setup.output_hint_asio4all: ASIO4ALL locks your whole interface, outputs included, so the metronome can't play through it. Pick a different output here (e.g. your computer's speakers), or turn off the interface's output in the ASIO4ALL panel and keep only its input.
setup.before_start_body: Pick your interface as the browser's microphone (mic icon in the address bar).

level.clipping: Clipping. Turn the input down on your interface

auto.no_signal: We didn't hear anything, so the sensitivity wasn't changed. Click again and keep playing for the whole measurement, the way you would in an exercise.
auto.clipping: Sensitivity set to {{gain}}×, but the signal clips before it reaches the app. Turn the gain down on your interface (or move the guitar away from the mic) and measure again.
auto.at_max: Even at the maximum ({{gain}}×) the guitar is quiet. Turn up the gain on your interface or move the mic closer.
auto.noisy: Sensitivity set to {{gain}}×, but the guitar barely stands out from the background noise. Sensitivity can't fix that. Quiet the room or move the mic closer to the guitar.

setup.ready: You can continue. The app hears your guitar.

output_stall.title: The metronome can't play
output_stall.body: Your audio driver is holding the output the app plays through, so the metronome and backing tracks can't be heard. Pick another output, e.g. your computer's speakers or headphone jack.
output_stall.asio4all: Using ASIO4ALL? In its panel, keep only your interface's input switched on, and make sure no other sound card is ticked there.

sustain.title: Sustain check
sustain.play: Play {{note}} on string {{string}}, fret {{fret}}, and let it ring.
sustain.clipping_live: Clipping. The input is too loud
sustain.pass: The app hears the note to the end. Tab notes will fill all the way.
sustain.gain: The note cut off after {{seconds}}s. Raise the sensitivity below and play it again.
sustain.quiet: The note faded out after {{seconds}}s. The signal is too weak. Turn up the gain on your interface (or move the mic closer) and play it again.
sustain.pitch: The pitch drifted off {{note}} after {{seconds}}s. Tune up or play it cleaner, then try again.
sustain.clipping: The signal clips before it reaches the app. Turn the gain down on your interface (or play softer) and play it again.
sustain.too_hot: The sensitivity is too high. The note pins the meter, and background noise will start passing for notes. Lower the sensitivity below (or set it automatically) and play it again.

source.title: Connect your guitar
source.question: How is your guitar connected to the computer?
source.mic_desc: Built-in laptop mic or external USB mic
source.mobile_body: Your phone's microphone will listen to your guitar.
source.mobile_headphones: Plug in headphones if you can
source.mobile_headphones_body: Without them the mic also hears the app's sounds from your speaker, and note detection gets less accurate.

summary.title: All set
summary.body: The app hears your guitar and will score your playing.
summary.latency_later: Measure it any time with the “Calibrate timing” button above the tab, so timing grades match what you hear.

permission.title: Microphone Access
permission.body: To detect your guitar notes, we need permission to use your audio input. No audio is ever recorded or sent to any server.

error.title: Microphone blocked
error.body: Please allow microphone access in your browser settings, then try again.

choice.title: Existing Calibration
choice.old: This calibration is over 30 days old. Consider recalibrating for best accuracy.

mic_mode.exam_body: This module requires microphone setup. Enable your microphone so the system can evaluate your playing during the exam.
mic_mode.body: This plan contains tablature exercises. Enable your microphone so the system can listen to your guitar and score your playing in real time.

timing_step.skip: Skip, the estimate will do for now
